ImageDescription.value:
For those who don't know, Bananas in Pyjamas was a very popular children's TV series in Australia during the 1990s.

I bought this camera for $1 (with $8 shipping) via that online auction website.

The camera has a plastic fixed-focus lens, a single shutter speed, a single aperture, and manual film advance. It operates without the need for batteries. It has no provision for flash. It was made in China. It appears related to the Panorama Wide Pic camera, though this is not a panoramic camera.

ObjectName.value: Liat Portal for Foodie Disorder - A Single Banana

Categories.value: Fruit|Food photography|Bananas|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value: High-quality photograph by Liat Portal showing a single ripe banana with natural surface marks, placed on a dark surface and photographed whole. The fruit is unpeeled and untouched, presented as found before consumption. This image documents prior to use, everyday eating, and reliable staple fruit, emphasizing food literacy and simple access to nutrition without preparation or cooking. Photographed in San Francisco. This image documents basic foods and repeatable daily choices as part of the Foodie Disorder global food culture archive.
